newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan President takes 25 pct salary cut.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan President takes 25 pct salary cut.

text.p: Taiwan's first directly-elected President Lee Teng-hui has taken a 25 percent cut in pay to avoid opposition parties' criticism, state media reported on Thursday.

It said Lee had asked to reduce his monthly income by T$200,000 (US$7,200) to T$616,500 ($22,400), while Vice-President Lien Chan had also offered to cut his pay by T$150,000 ($5,400) to T$465,800 ($17,000).
The cabinet accepted both offers on Thursday.
The Presidential Office declined to comment.
The opposition parties have criticised Lee's salary, saying it was nearly double that of U.S. President Bill Clinton.
Lee and Lien won the island's historic presidential election in March 1996 with a landslide 54 percent.
